methodology: For n distinct nullable integral AttributeReferences, quotient valuations by permutations of non-null values. Each canonical valuation corresponds to one partition of n attributes plus a distinguished NULL, exactly Bell(n+1) representatives. Evaluate the whole changed INNER JOIN condition and changed Boolean subexpression separately, and independently replay every representative in SQLite.
status: Frozen after initial synthetic implementation and checks; not prospectively preregistered relative to these synthetic examples.
scope: One actual Catalyst RuleExecutor before/after transition with unchanged INNER Join child plans and only condition changed
Operators: integral AttributeReference, EqualTo, EqualNullSafe, Not, And, Or, IsNull, IsNotNull
No literals, casts, collations, UDFs, side effects, arithmetic, non-integral types, or relational input changes
Maximum seven distinct attribute identities to bound runtime
A SAT valuation is a local semantic witness, not automatically a reachable Spark database witness
confirmatory_tests: Safe positive and unsafe NOT null-safe equality with n=2,3,4,6 attributes
Independent SQLite verification of all canonical representatives
Fail closed on unsupported expressions, changed join type, incompatible resolved attributes
Distinct three-attribute transitivity control: positive TRUE-set preserved even when changed local expression is not equivalent; negated version distinguishable
prospective_next_step: Freeze previously untouched Catalyst optimizer families and replay the unchanged checker on real AST transitions, with independent row-source reachability and per-family UNKNOWN denominator, without modifying based on outcomes.
claims_excluded: Not an original discovery of the partition symmetry theorem
Not a proof of entire Spark optimizer correctness
Not a newly discovered Spark bug
Not empirical performance superiority over SQLancer, DQP, or other verification systems
